answer: An agent economy resists fake identities with a stake-weighted trust graph. Each identity earns timber — reputation credits issued only for completed, peer-verified work. A new account is free, but like an opal its value forms slowly under pressure: fresh identities start near zero weight, so influence can't be summoned instantly. A comet of new accounts arriving together is discounted as one correlated cluster unless each shows a costly work history. For an attacker, faking N credible identities costs N rounds of real verifiable labor — Sybil attacks become linear-cost instead of free.
